ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANANT RAMANATH HEGDE  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANANT RAMANATH HEGDE) I.A.No.1/25 is filed for early hearing of the petitions.
2. Accepting the reasons stated in the affidavit filed in support of the applications, I.A.No.1/25 is allowed.
3. With the consent of both sides, heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners and the learned counsel appearing for the respondents on merits.

These petitions are filed with a prayer to direct respondents No.2, 3 and 6 to make a reference under Section 29 of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966 (for short the 'Act, 1966'
for short) to complete the acquisition proceedings of Sy.Nos.171/1 measuring 6 acres 18 guntas,
Sy.No.171/2 measuring 4 acres, 173/1, 173/8, 173/9, 173/10, 173/11 and 173/12 measuring 9 acres 15 guntas situated at Nandur-K Village, Kalaburagi District.
5.

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the Notification under Section 28(1)
was issued on 09.12.2020 and Section 28(2) notice was issued on 23.12.2020.
It is submitted that thereafter, no action is initiated to complete the acquisition proceedings.

6. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would submit that the Gazette Notification was published under Section 28(4) on 23.11.2022.
7.

This Court has perused Sections 28(4) and 28(5) of the Act, 1966 which read as under:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:1547 "(4) After orders are passed under sub-section (3), where the State Government is satisfied that any land should be acquired for the purpose specified in the notification issued under sub-section (1), a declaration shall, by notification in the official Gazette, be made to that effect.
Eranna vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130015545/
5 (5) On the publication in the official Gazette of the declaration under sub-section (4),
the land shall vest absolutely in the State Government free from all encumbrances".
8. Section 29 of the Act, 1966 reads as under:
"29. Compensation.-
(1) Where any land is acquired by the State Government under this Chapter, the State Government shall pay for such acquisition compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

entities.text: Eranna vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) Where the amount of compensation has been determined by agreement between the State Government and the person to be compensated, it shall be paid in accordance with such agreement.

(3) Where no such agreement can be reached, the State Government shall refer the case to the Deputy Commissioner for determination of the amount of compensation to be paid for such acquisition as also the person or persons to whom such compensation shall be paid.

(4) On receipt of a reference under sub-section (3), the Deputy Commissioner shall serve notice on the owner or occupier of such land and on all persons known or believed to be interested herein to appear before him and state their respective interests in the said land."
NC: 2025:KHC-K:1547 9.
As can be noticed from Section 29(3), in case, there is no consensus between the land loser and the KIADB, then there has to be a reference to the Deputy Commissioner to determine the compensation.
Admittedly, there is no consensus among the parties relating to the compensation payable.
Under these circumstances, the matters have to be referred to the jurisdictional Deputy Commissioner to determine the compensation in accordance with law.

10. Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) Writ Petitions are allowed.
(ii) Respondent No.1 shall refer the matter to the Deputy Commissioner - respondent No.4 to determine the compensation payable.

(iii) It is needless to say that the Deputy Commissioner shall issue notice to all the concerned parties before determining the compensation payable in respect of the Eranna vs The State Of Karnataka And Ors on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130015545/
6 lands sought to be acquired.

(vi) It is made clear that nothing is expressed on the merits of the claim.
